For the AA6111 HS2-T6 alloy, we use the Ludwik law to represent its flow behavior, while the elasticity is represented by a Young’s modulus of 70GPa and 0.33, which is typical for aluminum alloys. Since the bending direction, i.e. the tension side (the top surface) tensile direction, is along the L direction, we initially have used the Ludwik parameters fitted for the L-direction tensile samples (L02 or L03) in the bending simulations. The results of using the parameters of sample L03 (see Table 1), the bending loads calculated are similar to those of experiments initially, but the value increase faster. The calculated peak 16 load (2223N) is about 17% higher than those of experiments (~1900N) (see Fig. 15a). This could be due to deformation anisotropy. The bending deformation is in plane strain deformation mode with tension on the tension side and compression on the compression side, while uniaxial tension is closer to plane stress tension. The different deformation mode could lead to different dislocation accumulation rate and hence different work hardening rate. Therefore, the work hardening parameters need to be modified for bending deformation to reflect the strain mode difference with uniaxial tension.
